prompt:
Research the Chrome browser's officially documented release cycle (how many weeks between major stable releases, and the Extended Stable option). Cite the Chromium or Google page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the required source lines for the officially documented Chrome release cycle.

SOURCE: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/docs/process/release_cycle.md | QUOTE: "Chrome ships a new milestone (major version) to the stable channel every two weeks." | CLAIM: Chrome’s major Stable releases are shipped every two weeks.
SOURCE: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/docs/process/release_cycle.md | QUOTE: "Chrome Browser also maintains every fourth milestone branch for six additional weeks by backporting important security fixes to create an extended stable channel, where a new milestone is shipped every eight weeks." | CLAIM: Extended Stable is an eight-week major-release option that keeps one milestone longer and backports security fixes.
SOURCE: https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16942104 | QUOTE: "The Stable channel follows a 2-week release cycle, whereas the Extended Stable channel operates on an 8-week release cycle." | CLAIM: Google directly contrasts Stable as 2-week cadence with Extended Stable as 8-week cadence.
SOURCE: https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16942104 | QUOTE: "Extended Stable receives feature updates less frequently than Stable, but it continues to receive weekly refreshes for security fixes." | CLAIM: Extended Stable still gets weekly security refreshes even though feature milestones are less frequent.
